written.myAnswer: Draw a 3 cm vector from north towards east, at 60° to north, with the arrowhead in the direction of motion (using a scale of 100 m s⁻¹ = 1 cm).
Draw a 3.5 cm vector at 60° to the x-axis, with its arrowhead in the direction of the force (using a scale of 100 N = 1 cm).
A scalar quantity has magnitude only. A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
Scalars: distance, length, time, speed, and energy. Vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, weight, and force.
For head-to-tail addition, place the tail of each successive vector at the head of the previous one. The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last.
In scalar notation, a vector's direction is indicated by an arrow over its symbol.
Represent a vector by a straight line with an arrowhead. Draw its length to a chosen scale to show its magnitude; the arrowhead shows its direction.
